title: Le 3-5-7-9
rationale: The distinctive objective of winning the 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th tricks did not match a documented international game. Do not conflate it with poker's unrelated 3-5-7.

title: Le 500
rationale: This is Five Hundred: Euchre bowers, joker, kitty, trick contract and 500-point target. Cinq-Cent is a malformed singular spelling. This should be the canonical record over the later duplicate.

title: LE 8 AMÉRICAIN
rationale: The matching-suit/rank shedding game is the Crazy Eights family. Pagat recognizes the added regional names. Uno is a commercial descendant, not an alternative name for the standard-deck game.

title: All Fives
rationale: The rules match the two-player All Fives variant of All Fours. Cinch normally denotes Double Pedro, where both same-colour fives are scoring trumps, so it is not an exact alias here.

title: All Fours
rationale: High, Low, Jack and Game identify All Fours. Old Sledge and Seven Up are documented North American names; All Foes is the Trinidad name.

title: Allô Jack !
rationale: Players react to particular ranks with prescribed words or gestures; they do not call matching ranks as in Snap. This is the earlier canonical copy of the same core game as bonjour-monsieur.

title: L'Aluette
rationale: The 48-card pack, exceptional card hierarchy, partnerships and gestures identify Aluette, also called la Vache.

title: L'Ambigu
rationale: The em dash is a malformed placeholder alias. The two-stage deal, chances/combinations and betting describe the historical Ambigu, not any record sharing the placeholder.

title: Les Animaux
rationale: The face-up deal, matching ranks and calling an opponent's animal identify the Animals variant of Snap. The noise version is documented as Barnyard Snap; Animal Sounds is descriptive but not an established title.

title: L'Ascenseur
rationale: Changing hand sizes, exact trick bids, a turned trump and the hook rule identify Oh Hell. Elevator/L'Ascenseur is documented; Lift is only a literal translation. This is the preferred canonical record over beigne.

title: Le Baccara
rationale: Modulo-ten totals approaching nine identify Baccarat/Baccara. Baccarat Banque and Chemin de Fer are recognized but mechanically distinct Baccarat variants, not interchangeable aliases for a generic record.

title: La Banque Russe
rationale: The two packs, reserves, shared foundations/tableau and compulsory moves are exactly Russian Bank/Crapette. The database's crapette record has the same objective and mechanics.

title: La Banque
rationale: Three cards per punter and winning with a higher card of the dealer's turned suit match the Shoot/old Red Dog mechanism. chien-rouge describes the same comparison and betting rule. Banco is a Baccarat betting call, not a reliable game alias here.

title: Le Barbu
rationale: The changing negative and positive contracts, including avoidance of the king of hearts, identify Barbu. Related compendium games such as King and Canadian Salad are not aliases.

title: La Bassette
rationale: This is the historical banking game Bassette/Basset. Faro is historically related but not mechanically identical enough to add as an alias.

title: La Bataille Corse
rationale: Face-card payments plus reaction/slapping rules identify the Egyptian Ratscrew/Bataille Corse family. Tarot names a deck or a separate trick-taking game, not this ruleset.

title: Bataille Norvégienne
rationale: Three cards down, three up, three in hand, replenishing to three, equal-or-higher play, 2 resets and 10 clears identify Shithead. It is not War/Bataille. The later shithead record is the same game.

title: La Bataille
rationale: Simultaneously exposed cards, rank comparison and battles on ties are standard War/Bataille. This is distinct from Bataille Corse.

title: Le Baudet
rationale: The simultaneous construction of four ascending ace-to-king suit piles does not safely match Sevens, Domino, Nerts or another documented international ruleset. Preserve the two regional names only.

title: Le Beigne
rationale: The rising/falling deal sequence, exact bids and 10-plus-bid scoring are a standard Oh Hell variant. Scoring differences are normal variations, not a separate game identity.

title: La Belote
rationale: The 32-card pack, promoted trump jack and nine, contracts, declarations and belote-rebelote identify classical French Belote. Belot and Klaverjassen are related national games, not exact aliases.

title: La Bésigue
rationale: Two 32-card packs, trick play, marriages, bésigue melds and brisques identify Bezique/Bésigue. Chinese Bezique is a six-pack variant, not an alias. Besit/Bezit and Bézi are documented historical forms.

title: Black Jack
rationale: Flexible aces, ten-valued faces, player decisions before a bank dealer and a target of 21 are Blackjack/Twenty-One. vingt-et-un has the same rules. Le Valet Noir risks confusion with the unrelated British Crazy Eights name Black Jack.

title: Le Bog
rationale: The special board, pay-card pools, betting on pairs/triples/quartets and final stops phase identify Poch/Poque. Pagat explicitly records Bog as a French name. poque contains the same historical game.

title: Bonjour Monsieur, Bonjour Madame
rationale: The same rank-triggered greetings, salute and hand-on-pile actions occur in allo-jack; the additional number-card actions are house-rule extensions.

title: Le Boston de Nantes
rationale: The record describes the documented Boston de Nantes variant, with auction contracts, support and its own stake structure. Generic Boston remains a reasonable umbrella shorthand.

title: Le Bouchon
rationale: Passing cards to collect four of a kind followed by grabbing one fewer token than players is Spoons. Pagat explicitly identifies Bouchon as the French cork-token version.

title: La Bouillotte
rationale: Aucun is a malformed placeholder, not a name. Three-card hands, the turned card, brelan carré and historical betting structure identify Bouillotte.

title: Le Brag
rationale: Three-card combinations and Brag's continuing betting procedure identify Three Card Brag. Teen Patti is closely related but remains a separately named regional game.

title: Le Brelan
rationale: Three dealt cards, betting and a winning three of a kind describe historical Brelan. Bouillotte derives from it but has additional regulated betting and hand-ranking rules.

title: Le Bridge
rationale: Four-player partnerships, contract auction, declarer and dummy identify Contract Bridge. Rubber and Duplicate Bridge are formats of this game, not necessary aliases.

title: La Brusquembille
rationale: The historical French ace-ten trick game is Brusquembille; Bruxambille is a documented-looking orthographic form. Similar predecessors such as Briscan should not be merged without stronger rule evidence.

title: La Canasta Chinoise
rationale: The requirement for several canastas of specified kinds and a 15,000-point target makes this a distinct Canasta variant, not a duplicate of ordinary Canasta.

title: La Canasta
rationale: Two decks plus four jokers, same-rank melds, seven-card canastas and a 5,000-point target identify Classic Canasta.

title: La Carotte
rationale: The 28-card Quebec contract game with a four-card kitty and six-trick carotte contract did not safely match a documented international alias.

title: La Carte la Plus Basse
rationale: The rule that everyone plays their lowest card and the lowest wins is too generic to equate with the many unrelated games called Low Card. Retain only the attested French title.

title: Carte, s'il vous plaît !
rationale: The comma-separated title was malformed by the alias parser into Carte and s'il vous plaît !. Card Please is an unsupported literal translation, not a recognized English game name.

title: Le Cassino
rationale: Matching and additive captures, builds, most cards/spades and Big/Little Casino identify Casino. Casino and Cassino are both established spellings; the lowercase duplicate adds no alias value.

title: Le Charlemagne
rationale: Jokers, right/left bowers, kitty, trick bids, Mulot and Charlemagne contracts identify the eastern Canadian game. La Partie is generic and not corroborated by the established reference.

title: La Chasse à l'As
rationale: One card each, exchanging with the next player, king blocking exchanges and lowest card losing identify Cuckoo/Chase the Ace. Acey-Deucey is In Between, where a third card must fall between two cards. Pagat's Ace Chasing is also a different betting variant.

title: Le Chasse-Cœur
rationale: Avoiding hearts and the queen of spades, passing three cards and shooting the moon are standard Hearts/Black Lady. coeurs contains the same rules; dame-de-pique is another duplicate variant.

title: Le Chat
rationale: This game uses a single dealt packet, a central card, opponents' discard piles and penalties called chats. Spite and Malice instead uses personal reserve piles and shared ascending foundations, so the mechanics are materially different.

title: Le Château de Cartes
rationale: The physical dexterity game of adding cards on edge is clearly described, but Card Castle appears to be an unsupported literal translation rather than a recognized international title.

title: Le Chien Rouge
rationale: Betting that a hand contains a higher card of the dealer's turned suit is the original Red Dog/High Card Pool, not modern casino In Between. This should be canonical over banque.

title: Chkobba
rationale: The Tunisian 40-card game with compulsory matching/additive captures, chkobbas and its own scoring is Chkobba/Chkouba. Scopa is its Italian parent and Escoba captures to fifteen; they are related but mechanically distinct games.

title: Cinq Cents
rationale: The joker, Euchre bowers, kitty, trick auction and 500-point target are the same game as 500. Different player counts and pack sizes are standard Five Hundred variants.

title: Les Cinq Rois
rationale: Ordinary-card adaptation of the proprietary five-suit rummy game Five Crowns. No additional broadly recognized name was found.

title: Les Cœurs
rationale: The 26-point rules use hearts plus Q♠ and passing, identifying the modern Black Lady form usually called Hearts rather than original Hearts without Q♠.

title: Le Commerce
rationale: The rules combine a simple banking form with the historical trade-and-barter Commerce variant. Thirty-One and Stop the Bus are relatives, not exact aliases.

title: Commère, accommodez-moi
rationale: The two removals are punctuation-split title fragments, not independently documented game names. No reliable international equivalent was established.

title: La Conférence
rationale: Distinct old French 36-card partnership game with consultation, no trump, compulsory heading, and a five-trick undertaking. No reliable alternative name was found.

title: Le Coucou
rationale: Mechanics match the one-card Cuckoo or Ranter-Go-Round family: exchange with a neighbor, a king blocks, and the lowest card loses a life.

title: Le Couillon
rationale: The 24-card partnership rules and line-erasing score identify Belgian Couillon. Pagat documents the regional names Kwajongen, Kujong, and Troeven.

title: La Crapette Tarot
rationale: A tarot-pack competitive patience adaptation. It is related to Crapette, but its one-pack split layout differs enough to remain separate.

title: La Crapette
rationale: Rules match Russian Bank or Crapette: separate decks, reserve, eight foundations, compulsory plays, and loading the opponent. La is a parser fragment.

title: Le Cribbage
rationale: Standard six-card Cribbage to 121. Crib is already present, while the bare canonical form is missing.

title: La Dame de Pique
rationale: The rules are effectively identical to coeurs: passing, each heart scores 1, Q♠ scores 13, and there is no trump. La Dame de is a parser fragment.

title: Le Domino
rationale: French card Domino, where the first rank chosen becomes the starting rank for every suit. It is close to Sevens or Fan Tan but not necessarily identical.

title: Le Double Solitaire
rationale: The rules shuffle two decks together into eight rows of eight, unlike recognized competitive Double Solitaire, where each player has a separate Klondike layout. The title is not externally confirmed for these exact mechanics.

title: Dourak
rationale: Six-card Russian attack-and-defense shedding rules identify the common throw-in or Podkidnoy form of Durak.

title: L'Écarté
rationale: Standard two-player Écarté. The unaccented article form is malformed normalization; bare accented and conventional unaccented forms are preferable.

title: L'Élimination
rationale: This is a Québec betting game with five cards, rank-triggered discards, and high or low totals. Generic High-Low normally denotes other games and creates a false alias collision.

title: L'Enflé
rationale: References recognize these names for Enflé. The stored draw-until-suit rule is a substantial local variant of the usual pick-up-the-trick rule. The dash is placeholder data.

title: L'Euchre
rationale: Standard Euchre-family rules with five tricks and bowers. Eucre is a documented historical spelling; Jucker is an ancestor rather than an alias.

title: L'Extravagante Minoune
rationale: Québec Minoune variant using two joker packs and a dummy third hand. No reliable independent alternative name was found.

title: Les Familles
rationale: All cards are dealt, players request a specific card, and there is no fishing stock. These mechanics are Authors, with Quartett as a regional equivalent, not standard Go Fish or Pêche.

title: Le Fan Tan
rationale: Exact Sevens or Fan Tan layout beginning with sevens and building each suit both ways. This is not the unrelated Chinese casino game also called Fan-Tan.

title: La Ferme
rationale: A distinct French banking game targeting exactly 16. Aucun records the absence of an alias and is malformed data, not a name.

title: Le Flip
rationale: The simultaneous play onto two central piles matches Speed more closely than Spit. Lapsit could not be verified as a recognized name.

title: Le Florentin
rationale: Distinct banking game in which bettors back the appearance of the banker's starting rank. The dash is placeholder data, not an alias.

title: La Floune
rationale: Québec combination game using two wild jokers. No reliable independently documented alternative name was found.

title: Le Football Américain
rationale: Local two-player card simulation of American football. No established equivalent with matching mechanics was identified.

title: La Fouine
rationale: The stored four-player partnership and scoring rules do not match two-player Klaberjass or Kalabriasz. Those aliases belong to the separate kalabriasz entry.

title: Frappe le Valet
rationale: Exact Slapjack mechanics: cards are exposed in turn and the first player to slap a jack wins the pile.

title: Le Gin-Rami
rationale: Standard Gin Rummy with sets, runs, knocking, gin, deadwood, and undercut scoring.

title: Golf
rationale: The four face-down cards arranged as a square identify Four-Card Golf, also widely called Polish Poker.

title: Le Hoc
rationale: The combination phase followed by ascending sequences and payments for special cards identifies Hoc Mazarin.

title: L'Impériale
rationale: The unaccented smart-apostrophe form is malformed normalization. The stored long and abbreviated rules contradict each other, so no mechanical synonym is proposed.

title: Le In-Between
rationale: Players bet that a third card will rank between two initial cards, the standard In-Between or Acey-Deucey banking game.

title: Le Jeu de Loo
rationale: Standard Loo or Lanterloo structure: players must win a trick or pay into the pool.

title: Le Jeu des Valets
rationale: The no-trump avoidance game centered on the jack of spades is Polignac. Other jack-avoidance names often denote variants with different penalties.

title: Le Jeu du Roi
rationale: The ten-contract compendium with six negative and four positive deals matches King. Barbu, Kierki, Rıfkı, and Trex are related compendia rather than exact aliases.

title: Le Kalabriasz
rationale: The 32-card game with J-9 trump hierarchy, melds, bidding, and a 500-point target is the Klaberjass or Kalabriasz family. The additions are documented regional spellings.

title: Le Kilo de Plomb
rationale: Local five-player penalty game involving tricks, a stock, and recorded kilos. No reliable published equivalent was found.

title: Le Kilo
rationale: A local four-of-a-kind signaling game in the Pig or Spoons family, but those games are not exact aliases. The existing phrase is a parser fragment of the full local name.

title: Le Knock-Rummy
rationale: Basic Knock Rummy permits ending by knocking with sufficiently low unmatched cards. Poker Rum is a documented alternative name.

title: La Compliquée
rationale: A 104-card matching-memory variant requiring identical duplicate cards. Generic Memory, Concentration, and Pelmanism describe the parent game but are not exact aliases.

title: La Pomme
rationale: Unusual two-player trick game targeting 21 points within each trick. No established game with sufficiently matching mechanics was identified.

title: La Sélective
rationale: Local memory-game variant in which players complete five pairs from hidden cards. No independently documented exact synonym was found.

title: Le Lansquenet
rationale: Historical banking game in which the banker's and players' ranks compete as cards are exposed. Skin is its documented English form.

title: Le Front
rationale: Local bundle-capturing game where incomplete rank piles may be stolen. It resembles Stealing Bundles and Casita Robada but differs enough that neither is a safe exact alias.

title: Le Vicaire
rationale: The three-player, hearts-trump game does not match a recognized Vicar/Vicaire entry in major indexes. Retain only the documented local French name.

title: L'Échange
rationale: The two-player exchange-and-meld rules appear to be a local Quebec game related to La Minoune, not a recognized international game with a stable alternative name.

title: La Loterie
rationale: The two-deck lots-and-tickets mechanism is specific enough that the generic English translation Lottery should not be added without an established rules reference.

title: Le Macao
rationale: The rules are the historical banking game Macao: banker versus punters, objective nine, and immediate loss above nine. It is related to but mechanically distinct from Baccarat.

title: Mafia
rationale: Mafia and Werewolf/Loup-Garou are recognized themes of the same day/night social-deduction system. The database type Jeu de plis is incorrect but outside this name audit.

title: La Manille
rationale: The 32-card partnership rules and 10-A-K-Q-J ranking identify French Manille. Manilla/Malilla are related regional games rather than safe exact aliases.

title: Le Mariage Chinois
rationale: Turning two cards, retaining a rank match, replaying after success, and replacing failures is standard Concentration/Memory. The mechanics duplicate le-memory, not merely its aliases.

title: Le Mariage
rationale: The trick-and-draw game scores marriages and Ace-Ten counters and is historically within the Mariage/Brisque/Briscan family. These names are close historical forms, so no duplicate is asserted.

title: Le Marjolet
rationale: The 32-card trick-and-meld rules, marjolet trump jack, marriages, and brisques identify the recognized French game Marjolet.

title: Le « May I? »
rationale: The compulsory progressive melds and out-of-turn purchase of a discard identify May I?, a Contract Rummy variant. Contract Rummy is a family name, not an exact alias for this five-round ruleset.

title: La Mémoire à l'Épreuve
rationale: This is a scored Concentration derivative using exact duplicate cards and a separate point-card deck. The scoring apparatus is substantial enough to retain it as a named variant rather than mark an exact duplicate.

title: La Mémoire Collective
rationale: Its base play is standard Concentration: turn two, keep a match, otherwise replace them, with most pairs winning. Optional wild-card scoring does not distinguish the core record.

title: Le Menteur
rationale: Face-down rank claims, challenges, and taking the pile identify Cheat/Bullshit/I Doubt It. Pagat distinguishes this sequential-rank game from another same-rank game also called I Doubt It.

title: Le Michigan
rationale: The spare hand, ascending suit sequences, stop cards, pay cards, and first player out identify Michigan/Newmarket/Boodle. Chicago and Saratoga denote documented regional forms of the same Stops family.

title: Le Mille
rationale: The rules use ordinary three-of-a-kind melds, 2s as wild cards, a 1,000-point target, and no seven-card canastas or 5,000-point target. It is Canasta-related but not Canasta.

title: La Minoune
rationale: The same-rank melds, special queen-of-spades score, and Quebec terminology appear local. No reliable source established a broader alternative name.

title: La Mitaine
rationale: The bidding/capture game using mitaine, gant, and chausson combinations appears Quebec-specific. No reliable international synonym was found.

title: Le Motz
rationale: The unusual two-bower ranking and three-card optional-play mechanism resemble historical Rams-family games, but not closely enough to assign Mouche, Loo, or Rams as an alias.

title: La Mouche
rationale: The five-card draw/exchange trick game with a pool and penalty for taking no trick is historical Mouche. Bête, Mistigri, Pamphile, and Lanturlu are documented regional names/forms, though conventions vary.

title: Le Nain Jaune
rationale: The 7♦ pay compartment and ascending Stops play identify Nain Jaune/Yellow Dwarf. It is related to Michigan and Pope Joan but has a distinct board and pay-card structure.

title: Le Nap
rationale: Both records deal five cards, auction tricks through Nap/Wellington/Blücher, make the first lead trump, and settle by the contract. This is a mechanical duplicate of napoleon.

title: Le Neuf à Deux
rationale: The alternating keep/discard draft and fixed six-trick benchmark distinguish this Quebec game from standard exact-bid games. No additional established name was verified.

title: Le Neuf à Quatre
rationale: There is no bidding in these rules: both teams are measured against a fixed six-trick baseline. Oh Hell requires each player to bid an exact number of tricks, so it is not an alias.

title: Le Neuf à Trois
rationale: The fourth undealt/exchangeable hand and fixed four-trick benchmark are specific local mechanics. It should not be conflated with Oh Hell or 3-5-8.

title: Le Nigaud
rationale: The exposed personal piles and ascending placement onto another player's pile do not match a major indexed patience or shedding game closely enough for another alias.

title: La Papesse Jeanne
rationale: Removing 8♦, using 9♦ as Pope, eight staking compartments, a dead hand, and Stops play exactly identify Pope Joan. The two current plural Papesses forms are parser/spelling errors.

title: Le Papillon
rationale: The dash is a malformed placeholder alias. The fishing-by-equal-value-or-sum rules identify historical Papillon, but related games such as Cassino are not exact aliases.

title: Le Paquet Voleur
rationale: Four-card deals, rank matching, visible bundle tops, and stealing an opponent's whole bundle identify Stealing Bundles and its Argentine and Italian forms.

title: La Petite École
rationale: This is a ten-contract progressive rummy with local school/class terminology. It belongs to the Contract Rummy family, but its contract schedule is not identical to the existing generic or Frustration Rummy records.

title: La Petite Mémoire
rationale: Four face-down cards, initial inspection, draw-and-replace play, knocking, and lowest score are exactly Four-Card Golf. Different card values are ordinary Golf variations.

title: Les Petits Paquets
rationale: The dash is a placeholder and Les Petits is a malformed truncated alias. No reliable established alternative name was found for this banker-versus-packets game.

title: Le Pharaon
rationale: The banking layout and wagers on card outcomes identify the historical Pharaon/Faro family. Faro is not a duplicate of Macao: Faro wagers on ranks exposed in paired draws.

title: Pige dans le lac
rationale: Requesting ranks and drawing from the lake to complete books of four is Go Fish. It is not automatically a duplicate of familles, whose stored rules deal all cards and more closely resemble Authors.

title: Le Ping-Pong
rationale: The two-player comparison of pairs/triples with reusable captured cards appears to be a local named Battle derivative. No established international synonym was found.

title: Le Pinochle
rationale: The doubled 48-card deck, A-10-K-Q-J-9 order, marriages, arounds, Q♠-J♦ meld, and trick points identify Pinochle. Pinocle and Penuchle are documented spellings.

title: Le Pique
rationale: Four players in partnerships, bids for tricks, and spades permanently trump identify Spades. The French names are transparent established renderings of that game.

title: Le Piquet
rationale: Two players, 32 cards, exchange from an eight-card talon, declarations, and tricks identify classic Piquet; the prevalent six-deal form is Rubicon Piquet.

title: Le Plus-d'Atouts
rationale: The game is a simple historical comparison of the number of trumps held after a partial deal. No reliable English or international alternative name was established.

title: Le Poker Menteur
rationale: The stored game passes one five-card hand while announcing successively stronger poker combinations. The recognized English game Liar's Poker instead bids on digits in banknote serial numbers, so that alias is misleading.

title: Le Poker
rationale: The primary stored rules deal five private cards, allow an exchange, and have betting before and after it: Five-Card Draw. Texas Hold'em uses community cards and is a variant, not an alternative name.

title: Le Polignac
rationale: Both database records use the same 28–32-card reverse trick game, penalize captured jacks with J♠ worth two, and share the names Polignac/Jeu des Valets.

title: La Politaine
rationale: Its 10-9-A ranking, eleven-point deal, steck, signalling conventions, and 10-9-A combination distinguish it from Manille despite superficial similarities. No reliable alternative name was found.

title: Le Poque
rationale: Aucun is a malformed no-alias placeholder. The pay compartments, vying on pairs/triples/quartets, and final Stops phase identify Poch/Poque/Bog; the stored bog record has the same three-phase structure.

title: Le Pot
rationale: The three-card hand, six-card exchange pot, three exchange rounds, and requirement for a set or sequence did not match a reliably documented game closely enough for another name.

title: Le Pouilleux
rationale: Discarding rank pairs and losing by retaining the unmatched jack is the French male-card form of Old Maid. Vieux Garçon, Black Peter/Schwarzer Peter, and Papaz Kaçtı are recognized national forms with the same mechanism.

title: La Poule à 3 Cartes
rationale: The stored rules are a three-trick trump game with exchanges and compulsory overtake/cut. Three Card Brag is a vying game based on poker combinations, not this game.

title: La Poule à 5 Cartes
rationale: The stored rules use five trump tricks and award the pot by tricks won. Five Card Brag is a poker-like vying game, so the shared card count does not establish identity.

title: La Préférence
rationale: The fixed suit hierarchy and six-trick contract identify Central European/Austrian Preference. Russian Preferans is a later game with contracts from six through ten tricks. 'Le Préférence' has the wrong French article.

title: Le Président
rationale: The rules are the climbing game President. Pouilleux is an Old Maid-type pairing game with an unmatched card; Pallmall is not corroborated as a recognized President name.

title: Le Puits
rationale: The English name appears to be an unsupported literal translation rather than a documented international alias. No reliable reference was located for this exact seven-card shedding rule.

title: Le Quarante-Cinq
rationale: Forty-Fives/45s is descended from Spoil Five but is separately named and scored to 45. Spoil Five is the ancestor, not a strict alias.

title: Le Quatre-Quatorze
rationale: The Quebec numeric form 4-14 is internally consistent with the dual-target rules. No established English or international name was reliably corroborated.

title: Le Quatre-Vingt-Dix-Neuf
rationale: This is the addition/shedding game where the running total must not exceed 99. It is distinct from the trick-taking game also called Ninety-Nine.

title: Le Quit
rationale: The em dash is a malformed placeholder alias. The rules require a proprietary 56-card pack; no independent alternative name was found.

title: Le Rami
rationale: The mechanics are basic draw-and-discard Rummy: sets/runs and going out, without the defining discard-pile access and cumulative scoring of 500 Rummy.

title: Le Rams
rationale: Five-card opt-in trick play, a widow and penalties identify the Rams family. Ramsch is context-sensitive because it also names a Skat contract, but is documented as a Rams name.

title: La Réussite
rationale: The page is an umbrella for patience/solitaire games. Most current names are individual layouts or variants, not alternative names for the category itself.

title: Le Reversi
rationale: The 48-card, no-trump trick-avoidance game is historical Reversis, not the board game Reversi. Standalone 'Le' is a malformed parser alias.

title: Le Roi et son Épée
rationale: The current forms are orthographic variants. No reliable established alternative name was located for this exact king-and-ace pairing game.

title: Le Rouge contre le Noir
rationale: The stored rules describe a two-player trick game scoring cards of a selected color, not casino Rouge et Noir or Trente-et-Quarante. No reliable alternative name was found.

title: Le Rummy 500
rationale: The buried-discard pickup rule, 7/13-card deal and target of 500 match the separate rami-500 page essentially rule for rule. Pinochle Rummy, not Rummy Pinochle, is documented.

title: Le Rummy Baltimore
rationale: This is a five-deal contract-rummy form with out-of-turn buying. It is related to Contract Rummy and May I?, but its schedule does not justify treating those broader games as exact aliases.

title: La Salade
rationale: The six phases include a fifth Domino/Fan-Tan-style shedding hand with wild cards. This differs from Canadian Salad, whose fifth hand penalizes the last trick; Mixed Hearts is misleading.

title: Le Sans-Cœur
rationale: The stored page labels Jeu du Roi as a confusion. Its five-phase, 32-card structure differs from the database's ten-deal jeu-du-roi and from ordinary Hearts.

title: La Scopa
rationale: The rules match Italian Scopa. Escoba and Chkobba are related regional games with changed capture/scoring rules, not strict aliases.

title: Le Sept et Demi
rationale: The 7½ banking game is internationally documented under Italian, English and Spanish names with equivalent half-point court-card mechanics.

title: Le Sept-Vingt-Sept
rationale: The Quebec numeric alias is consistent with the two target totals. No recognized English name for these exact rules was reliably corroborated.

title: Shithead
rationale: The 3-down/3-up/3-hand layout, beating pile, special 2 and 10, and last-player loss identify Shithead. Pagat documents the additions; generic Shed is not corroborated there.

title: La Sixte
rationale: The em dash is a malformed placeholder. No reliable alternative name was found for this six-player, 36-card trick game.

title: Le Skat
rationale: The main rules are ordinary Skat. Räuber/Rauber Skat is a specific variant and should not be indexed as an alternative name for standard Skat.

title: Le Skyjo
rationale: Skyjo is the product's established name. No recognized translated alternative name is needed.

title: Snap
rationale: Stored rules award matching exposed ranks after calling Snap. Slapjack awards the center pile for slapping Jacks and is separately represented by frappe-le-valet/le-slapjack mechanics.

title: Snip Snap Snorem
rationale: Snorem/Snorum are documented spellings. This page uses the equal-rank form; snip-snap-snoru uses the five-card sequence form. Pagat treats both as forms of the game, but their mechanics differ materially.

title: Le Solitaire à Deux
rationale: Two separate Klondike layouts racing onto shared foundations are Double/Simultaneous Solitaire. The database's double-solitaire is a single shuffled 104-card 8×8 patience, so it is not a rules duplicate.

title: Stud à 5 Cartes
rationale: One hole card followed by four exposed cards and betting rounds is standard Five Card Stud.

title: Stud à 7 Cartes
rationale: Two down/one up, four further streets, and the best five-card hand from seven identify standard Seven Card Stud.

title: Le Tarot
rationale: The 78-card deck, chien, bouts/oudlers and French contract thresholds identify French Tarot specifically, rather than tarot card games generally.

title: Le Tennis
rationale: No reliable established international alternative name was located for the exact card simulation described.

title: La Tontine
rationale: Card actions, circulating jetons, death/resurrection and last survivor match historical Tontine. The em dash is a malformed placeholder.

title: Le Treize
rationale: Standalone Québec is a parser fragment from the parenthetical qualifier. Thirteen deals with a changing wild rank identify a rummy game, not the banking treize page.

title: Le Jeu du Treize
rationale: This is a banking/counting game in which thirteen ranks are called against thirteen exposed cards. It is mechanically unrelated to treize-quebecois despite the shared short name.

title: Le Trente-et-Quarante
rationale: The casino tableau with Noir/Rouge and Couleur/Inverse bets is internationally known as Trente et Quarante, Thirty and Forty, or Rouge et Noir.

title: Le Trente-et-Un
rationale: The rules are a banker-versus-pontes draw-to-31 game. Thirty-One is a defensible translation but is ambiguous internationally because several unrelated games use that name.

title: La Triomphe
rationale: Five-card hands, turned trump, compulsory following/trumping and three tricks to win match historical Triomphe/French Ruff.

title: Le Valet de Trèfle
rationale: The trump order and melds resemble the Jass/Belote family, but the target and card values do not cleanly match Belote, Klaberjass or Klaverjas. No alias should be inferred from family resemblance alone.

title: Le Vingt-et-un
rationale: The main rules describe traditional rotating-banker Twenty-One, with Blackjack only as a later variant. Casino Blackjack and Pontoon have materially distinct rules; shared ancestry does not make them exact aliases or duplicates.

title: Vive la Joie
rationale: Rules support the local equivalence to Dernier Valet: discard rank-pairs, draw blindly from a neighbor, and win by emptying the hand. It resembles Old Maid but lacks the defining unmatched loser card.

title: Le Whip
rationale: Le ip is a parser corruption caused by dropping Wh, and the em dash is a placeholder. Mechanics are a Flemish fishing game related to Cassino/Scopa, but its scoring and covering rules do not justify those aliases.

title: Le Whist à la Couleur
rationale: Auctions include emballage, solo, misère, piccolo and abondance, identifying the continental color-contract variant rather than simple Whist. It is not mechanically identical to the whist page's main game.

title: Le Whist
rationale: The main rules are classic partnership Whist with turned trump, tricks above six and honors. Le ist is parser corruption. Prussian Whist and Whist à la couleur are variants, the latter with separate auction mechanics and its own page.

title: GIN RUMMY
rationale: Same 10-card knock-rummy mechanics as gin-rami: sets/runs, deadwood, knock, gin and undercut. The house rule incorrectly allows Q-K-A, whereas standard Gin Rummy keeps the ace low, but this is a rules error rather than a distinct game.

title: LE KEM'S
rationale: Mechanics exactly match Kemps: simultaneous exchanges, four of a kind, partner signal and counter-call. 'Jeu des Mots' is unrelated; 'Kem' appears to be a truncated parser alias. Carré-Coupé, Cash and Gemsch are documented regional forms.

title: Le Paquet de Merde
rationale: The stored rules reproduce Kilo de Merde: four-card rank sets, passing one card around, touching the central pile, kilo penalties and a flush-clearing card. Differences in starting player and whether 7 or 8 clears penalties are minor house variations.

title: RAMI 500
rationale: Same game as rummy-500: cumulative 500-point target, table melds, laying off and taking a buried discard together with all cards above it.

title: Régicide
rationale: Official international title is Regicide; Régicide is the natural French spelling. Mechanics match the published cooperative game against Jacks, Queens and Kings.

title: Yaniv
rationale: The rules are recognizably Yaniv. Pagat documents Jhyap and Dhumbal in Nepal and Kluft in the Netherlands. No reliable established use was found for 'Main Verte' or 'Yanoff'; both look like local or corrupted aliases.

title: Anandis
rationale: Distinct two-player deduction game using 16 court cards, a joker and one hidden card. No established international alternative name was located.

title: Animals
rationale: An animal-name variant of Snap. Barnyard Snap is the documented animal-sound form. It should not be marked duplicate of ordinary Snap because the memorized identities or sounds are a material mechanic.

title: Basra
rationale: Pagat documents Assaba-al'-Komi and Ashush as regional names. Pâsur, Kontsina and Tablić are related fishing games, not safe aliases: capture powers and scoring differ.

title: Big Three
rationale: Pagat confirms Big Three/Da San and Dig a Hole/Wa Keng for the Shaanxi climbing game. It is related to Dou Dizhu but has different cards, rankings and legal combinations.

title: Blanche-Neige
rationale: A distinct role-dependent shedding design. It is derived from Crazy Eights/8 Américain but the five asymmetric character rules prevent treating those family names as aliases.

title: Brain Drain
rationale: David Parlett arithmetic game using four operands to reach a fifth target card. It is derived from Twenty-Four but changes the target, scoring and card values, so it is not a duplicate.

title: C.Q.F.D.
rationale: The punctuation is intentional and not a malformed alias: C.Q.F.D. expands to Cartes Qu’il Faut Deviner in the rules. No other established name was found.

title: Camicia
rationale: Italian Beggar-my-Neighbour-family game in which A, 2 and 3 impose payment counts. Family labels such as Beggar-my-Neighbour and Bataille Corse should not be aliases because their attack cards and slap rules differ.

title: Candyman
rationale: Winking hidden-role game with Candyman, police officer and buyers. It is related to Wink Murder/Killer, but the specific roles, win conditions and card assignment make a duplicate claim unsafe.

title: Cinquante Plus/Moins
rationale: Locally documented arithmetic game attributed to Dani. The translated forms are useful search variants but were not independently established; no mechanics-equivalent database game was identified.

title: Clubbed
rationale: Named invention by Dave and Kendall Cline. Although its matching rule resembles Crazy Eights, clubs transfer the entire discard pile to the opponent and victory depends on the smallest captured stock.

title: Color Game
rationale: Simple red/black prediction game. Colour Game is only the British spelling; no distinctive established international title was found.

title: Colour-blind
rationale: David Parlett design. Added only punctuation and British/American spelling forms; no separate mechanics-equivalent title was found.

title: Crapaud
rationale: The rules explicitly identify Toad as the original English title. 'Le' is a malformed article-only parser alias.

title: Démocratie
rationale: The Cleveland game is described under the translated French title Démocratie; Democracy is the natural original-language form. Its simultaneous tribal voting tricks are distinctive.

title: Dingo
rationale: Distinct Cleveland hunt game with rabbits, dingoes and wolves mapped to suits. No reliable alternative title was found.

title: East-West
rationale: Reiner Knizia design predating Schotten Totten/Battle Line. Those later games are relatives, not aliases; East West is only a punctuation variant.

title: Éleusis
rationale: Both accented French and unaccented international forms are already present. New Eleusis and Eleusis Express are materially revised variants and should not be added as exact aliases.

title: Fotboll
rationale: Roland Johansson's Swedish football-simulation card game. Football is the direct translated title documented by the rule source; no database duplicate matches its field layout and attack sequence.

title: Horse Race
rationale: Matches Pagat's Basic Horse Race exactly: four aces, seven-card course, suit-driven movement and bookmaker odds. 'Racing Aces' was not added because that name is also used for materially different layouts.

title: Identité
rationale: Distinct memory/deduction design involving forehead cards and a matching memory grid. Identity is a translation/search form, not independently corroborated as a published title.

title: Kontsina
rationale: Pagat confirms all three Greek transliterations. Basra and Casino are relatives, not duplicates: Kontsina permits only one equal-sum combination and uses its own five-point scoring.

title: La Famille Cœur
rationale: A one-family adaptation of Happy Families/Jeu des 7 familles. It should remain distinct because it uses only six named heart cards and a specific request script.

title: La Salade Canadienne
rationale: The source explicitly gives Grande Salade; Canadian Salad is the established English rendering. Barbu is a related compendium but differs in contracts and structure.

title: La Triche
rationale: The stored mechanics exactly match Pagat's ascending-rank Cheat/I Doubt It and the existing menteur entry: face-down claims, cyclic ranks and challenges. This is not the separate same-rank version also called Bluff/I Doubt It.

title: Last One
rationale: A specific Crazy Eights-family variant with 4-7 mêlée sequences and its own scoring. Generic names such as Crazy Eights, Last Card and 8 Américain would overmerge mechanically different games.

title: Le 100
rationale: Matches Pagat's One Hundred adding game, including black aces, spade 2, red 5s, 10, Jack, heart Queen and Kings. Related 98 and 99 games have different limits and card effects.

title: Le 14
rationale: Distinct shedding game based on making and rearranging combinations totalling 14 across four staged packets. No independently established alternative title was found; Fourteen is only a translation/search form.

title: Le 21
rationale: The source explicitly identifies Stack Cards. Although inspired by Blackjack, this is a cooperative four-pile puzzle with combination scoring, not Blackjack itself.

title: Le 24
rationale: Same arithmetic puzzle documented internationally: use four card values exactly once with basic operations to make 24. The stored two-player shedding format is a documented long-game form, not a different game.

title: Le 41
rationale: The rules explicitly identify the Indonesian name Empat Satu. It resembles same-suit draw-and-discard games but has four cards and subtractive off-suit scoring, so Thirty-One is not an alias.

title: Le 51 Japonais
rationale: The Japanese name Goju Ichi is explicitly documented. The five-card market and subtractive off-suit scoring distinguish it from Chinese 51 and other commerce games.

title: Le 7 de Cœur
rationale: A playing-card implementation of Jeu de l'Oie with the heart 7 as finish. Jeu de l'Oie describes the inspiration, not an alternative name for this exact card layout.

title: Le 7½
rationale: Same banking game as sept-et-demi: 40 cards, courts worth one-half, target 7½ and banker winning ties. Pagat confirms the Italian, Spanish, Portuguese and English names.

title: Le 98
rationale: Matches Pagat's standard 98 exactly: four-card hands, running total, 10 as -10, J/Q as zero and King setting 98. It is related to but not identical with 99 and 100.

title: Le Bingo
rationale: Standard playing-card adaptation of Bingo using one deck as player cards and another as caller deck. Generic Bingo is acceptable, but this should not be merged with numbered bingo implementations.

title: Le Cabo
rationale: A specifically documented simplified Cabo variant. It shares the Golf/Tamalou family and much of le-tamalou's layout, but differs materially in powers, matching from opponents' layouts, scoring and end conditions; therefore no duplicate designation.

title: Le Cuttle
rationale: Mechanics match established Cuttle: point cards, scuttling, one-off effects, permanent royals and a 21-point goal. Cutthroat Cuttle is the documented three-player variant.

title: Le Générala
rationale: Camerounian elimination trick game with inability-to-follow penalties and Jokers as highest cards. It is unrelated to the Latin American dice game also called Generala; no other card-game name was corroborated.

title: Le Go Fish
rationale: Same asking, fishing and four-of-a-kind mechanics as the existing record. Current alias has a parser-added article.

title: Le Go Fish Deluxe
rationale: Pair-collecting variant documented by Pagat as Australian Fish; materially different from ordinary Go Fish. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Gops
rationale: Pagat explicitly documents both Goofspiel spellings and the acronym expansion. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le James Bond
rationale: Pagat lists the regional names for the same simultaneous four-of-a-kind packet game. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Killer
rationale: The hidden murderer kills by winking while a detective identifies them, matching Wink Murder. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Kilo de Merde
rationale: Distinct scored passing-and-reaction game. Bouchon is only a documented equipment variant and is not safe as an alias because a separate Bouchon record exists. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Kings Corners
rationale: Pagat recognizes Kings Corners and Kings in the Corners for the same shedding layout game. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Knock-out Whist
rationale: All alternatives are explicitly listed by Pagat for the diminishing-hand elimination game. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Memory Coopératif
rationale: Cooperative adaptation of Memory/Concentration, not the competitive Memory record. English forms are descriptive translations rather than strongly established titles. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Memory
rationale: Pagat identifies all four names for the same pair-matching memory game. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Neuf
rationale: Modern authored battle game by Yusuf and Yaqub; no independently recognized alternative title found. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Poker Squares
rationale: The 5x5 fixed-placement and ten-hand scoring mechanics match the recognized solitaire under all three names. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Rami Contrat
rationale: Its seven contracts, changing hand sizes and 'May I?' rule match Pagat's Contract Rummy. Liverpool Rummy, May I?, Shanghai Rummy and Progressive Rummy have rule differences and are not added as aliases. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Rami Frustration
rationale: Fourteen-contract rummy related to Progressive and 12-Step Rummy, but its exact contract schedule is distinct. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Rami Machiavel
rationale: Two decks without jokers, thirteen-card hands and unrestricted rearrangement of table melds match Pagat's Italian Machiavelli. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Slapjack
rationale: Players slap only jacks and collect the pile. The existing snap record matches equal ranks instead, so its shared Slapjack alias does not make these duplicates. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Snap Irlandais
rationale: Called ranks, matching and last-to-slap penalties identify Irish Snap, not ordinary Snap or Slapjack. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Tamalou
rationale: Four hidden cards, two initial peeks, low-score call, power cards and matching identify the power-card Golf/Cabo family. le-cabo-var has materially different powers and scoring, so it is a related variant rather than a duplicate. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Le Yami
rationale: Max Gerchambeau's scored sixteen-round hybrid of Yahtzee/Yam's, rummy and poker; no established alternative title found. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Les 7 Familles
rationale: French family-collection game recognized by Pagat as Jeu des Sept Familles. Happy Families is related but uses different family composition and is not treated as an exact alias. Current alias has a leading article.

title: Littérature
rationale: Pagat explicitly lists the English and North American names for the partnership half-suit game.

title: Marguerite
rationale: Custom hidden-card deduction game; no recognized international alternative name found. It should not be conflated with generic missing-card or Cluedo-style games.

title: Mustamaija
rationale: Finnish beating game. Black Maria is only a translation/comparison and Pagat explicitly says the British Black Maria game is mechanically different.

title: Napoléon
rationale: Five-card British trick auction with Two, Three, Misère, Four, Nap, Wellington and Blücher is the same game as existing nap, not Japanese Napoleon.

title: Noddy
rationale: Historical English adding game and precursor of Cribbage; no established alternative title found.

title: Omben
rationale: Pagat documents Omben as the Javanese name and Minuman as the Indonesian name for this specific Go Fish variant.

title: Oracle
rationale: Peter Higgins deduction/guessing design; no independently recognized alternative name found.

title: Pâsur
rationale: Pagat explicitly documents these Iranian names for the same eleven-sum fishing game; accentless transliterations improve international searchability.

title: Pig
rationale: Pagat treats Pig and Spoons as closely grouped forms of the same four-of-a-kind passing game and documents Hog and Donkey regionally. Bouchon changes the token and penalty convention, so the existing Bouchon record is not marked as a duplicate.

title: Promenade
rationale: Custom card-board race involving fruit cards, a die and pawns; no established alternative title found.

title: Q Squared Joe NG
rationale: New Game combat design with hands, resources and hidden terrain. Its mechanics differ substantially from both Q Squared Joe and Q Squared Joe War.

title: Q Squared Joe War
rationale: Battlefield combat derivative with exploited cards and attacks; mechanically distinct from the classic shedding game and NG version.

title: Q Squared Joe
rationale: The source explicitly gives Q²J as the abbreviated name. This is a shedding game, unlike its War and NG derivatives.

title: Quads
rationale: Brooke Nicole Shell's simultaneous central-market four-of-a-kind game; no reliable alternative title found. It is not Pig, James Bond or Kemps despite the shared four-of-a-kind objective.

title: Sab’at Al-Deemin
rationale: Arabic transliteration variants and literal translations. Although related to Domino/Fan Tan, this Saudi partnership game starts every suit at seven and builds upward only, with distinct scoring.

title: Seven Spades
rationale: Johan Wästlund bluff game; Sept Piques is the documented French translation. No broader established alias found.

title: Shamus
rationale: Distinct cooperative hybrid assigning Uno-like and Rummy-like roles against a ten-card timer; no recognized alternative name found.

title: Snip Snap Snorum
rationale: Assigned rules use five-card ascending suit sequences. Existing snip-snap-snorem instead uses four equal ranks, so the shared historical name does not establish a duplicate.

title: Spit
rationale: Five exposed stock piles and simultaneous adjacent-rank play identify Spit. Speed is closely related but uses five-card hands and one stock pile, so it is not added as an exact alias.

title: Stortok
rationale: Pagat documents Kjempetosk as the Norwegian equivalent of the Swedish two-trump beating game.

title: Thinkabit
rationale: Reiner Knizia memory game using five-card poker combinations; no reliable alternative title found.

title: Trash
rationale: Pagat explicitly lists Garbage and Ten for the Ace-to-Ten positional layout game.

title: Tres y Dos
rationale: Recognized Caribbean draw-and-discard game whose exact objective is a full house. Generic Full House is not added because it is not established as the game's name.

title: Wizard Duel
rationale: Modern authored attack-and-defense game with suit-specific defensive effects; no reliable alternative title found.

title: LE TOUR DE FRANCE
rationale: Explicit house rule with ten-centered suit foundations, time scoring and a special fifth round. It resembles stops/foundation games but is not mechanically identical. Current alias is malformed by leading article and all-caps parser output.
